### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, touching **5** documentable anchor(s).

**32** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 600b1e2ab129008e9d43e7101be35d22befe2142`.

⛔ **8** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `os validate (command, 49 pages)`
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **215** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **155** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **155**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **100** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.

Coarse fallback — **24** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 600b1e2ab129008e9d43e7101be35d22befe2142` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `1664c593ba7ce4cc55ff6bdb9755600cf4521776` — the merge of head `6a0a4df1b4e9e2f83578c2278f5985fc0053e74c` into base `600b1e2ab129008e9d43e7101be35d22befe2142`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 1664c593ba7ce4cc55ff6bdb9755600cf4521776 && git checkout 1664c593ba7ce4cc55ff6bdb9755600cf4521776
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 600b1e2ab129008e9d43e7101be35d22befe2142 6a0a4df1b4e9e2f83578c2278f5985fc0053e74c && git checkout -B drift-repro 600b1e2ab129008e9d43e7101be35d22befe2142 && git merge --no-ff 6a0a4df1b4e9e2f83578c2278f5985fc0053e74c

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 600b1e2ab129008e9d43e7101be35d22befe2142
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 600b1e2ab129008e9d43e7101be35d22befe2142` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

### The failing assertion, recovered locally — CI could not hand it over

<sub>`domain:cli` execution PM seat · reading 2026-09-18T04:25Z · reproduced at this PR's head `15cc0db8d4`</sub>

`Test Core (4/6)` is red at step 11. ⛔ The job log is **not readable from this container** — it redirects off `api.github.com` to `productionresultssa*.blob.core.windows.net`, which this session's egress refuses (`http=000`, no bytes). That is an absence of a **reading**, not an absence of evidence, so the assertion below was recovered by running the shard rather than by guessing from the annotations.

What CI did publish, as annotations:

```
exit-status      Process completed with exit code 1.
package-pointer  command (…/packages/cli) pnpm run test --shard=2/2 exited (1)
```

Re-run here, whole, with **no `--project` filter** — which is what `packages/cli`'s `"test"` script (`vitest run`) does on CI:

```
Test Files  2 failed | 131 passed (133)
Tests       1 failed | 1611 passed | 15 skipped (1627)

FAIL |integration| test/build-text-face-advisory-count.test.ts
  > #18780 — `os build`'s text face prints every advisory its summary line counts
  > the fixture reaches the per-package pass and raises a survivor there

  test/build-text-face-advisory-count.test.ts:239
    expect(perPackage.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
  AssertionError: expected 0 to be greater than 0
```

**What it is.** That is a **precondition** test, not a count pin: it asserts #18780's fixture really reaches the per-package pass and leaves a survivor, so the equality assertions below it are not vacuous. On that fixture the only per-package survivor **was the echo** — so once this PR's key stops letting echoes through, the count is 0 and the precondition fails.

⇒ Same shape as the `#18677` validate-parity fixture this PR already repaired, in a third file. The remedy is the same one and it is **not** relaxing the assertion: give the fixture a survivor **the union genuinely cannot see** — a field whose only consumer lives in a sibling package. ⛔ Weakening `toBeGreaterThan(0)` would re-open the very defect #18780 exists to close.

**Why a green local run and a red CI coexisted.** The failing test is `|integration|` tier. The delivering run covered `--project unit` (216 files) plus only the two integration parity files this diff touches, so this file was never collected locally. ⇒ validation before the next push is `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli test` **whole**, not a file list.

**One reading in that run is NOT this PR's, recorded so nobody chases it.** `test/published-subpath-hook-body.pin.test.ts` failed at load with the file's own deliberate refusal — *"packages/cli is not built (./dist/index.js is absent) … Run: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli build`"*. This worktree built `@objectstack/cli^...`, the dependency closure, and not the package itself. ⛔ A gap in my environment, not a defect, and not in this PR's scope.

⇒ **One real failure, one file, one fixture to repair.** The fix is in progress; this comment exists so the assertion is on the record, since the job log that carries it cannot be fetched.
